s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually developing skin lesion with verrucous appearance and soft-tissue mass
salient_findings: Slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple
Translucent papules and plaques with surface hemorrhagic crust
Papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration of small round blue cells
key_facts: Asymptomatic skin lesion on the right temple
No associated fevers, weight loss, or night sweats
Lesion is nontender with no purulent discharge
Imaging studies revealed skin thickening and a soft-tissue mass in the right frontotemporal region
Histopathology showed papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration
Tumor cells are positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin

shortlist.label: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Verrucous appearance of the skin lesion and gradual development over 8 months

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Neoplastic infiltration consisting of small round blue cells and positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma

raw.rationale: The tumor cells are positive for MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, and desmin, which are markers for rhabdomyosarcoma, and the histopathology shows papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration consistent with embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma

rejected.label: Verrucous carcinoma
rejected.why: While the lesion has a verrucous appearance, the immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of verrucous carcinoma

rejected.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, but the specific subtype is more likely given the clinical and histopathological features

rejected.label: Pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: This subtype typically occurs in adults and has a more pleomorphic appearance on histology, which is not consistent with the described case

rejected.label: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: This subtype typically has a distinct alveolar pattern on histology and is often associated with a worse prognosis, which is not consistent with the described case
